en.title: Telling the time
en.summary: We tell the time with numbers and the small words past, to, half, quarter and o'clock.

paragraphs: We tell the time with the numbers on the clock and a few small words: past, to, half, quarter and o'clock. The question is What time is it? or What's the time? We answer with It is, followed by the time. In everyday speech we often round to the nearest five minutes.

For the minutes up to thirty use past, and after thirty use to. The hour comes last: ten past two, twenty to five. At fifteen minutes we say a quarter, and at thirty we say half past. Americans often say after instead of past. In timetables and in writing, a.m. and p.m. or the 24-hour clock may be used.

blocks.html:
TimeSay
7:00seven o'clock
7:15a quarter past seven
7:30half past seven
7:45a quarter to eight
7:55five to eight

paragraphs: We can also say the numbers directly: seven fifteen, seven forty-five. This is common for digital clocks, timetables and announcements. For minutes below ten we say oh: seven oh five.
To give the time of an event, use at: The film starts at nine. To say about, use around: around noon. Noon means twelve o'clock in the day and midnight means twelve at night.

items: Wrong: **It is half to eight.** Right: **It is half past seven.**
Wrong: **It is seven hours.** Right: **It is seven o'clock.**
Wrong: **in nine o'clock** Right: **at nine o'clock**

ro.title: Cum spunem ora
ro.summary: Spunem ora în limba română cu verbul „a fi”, numere și câteva cuvinte scurte.

paragraphs: În română, întrebăm simplu: „Cât e ceasul?” sau „Cât este ceasul?”. Răspundem de obicei cu verbul „este” sau cu forma scurtă „e”. Folosim numerele și cuvinte precum „și”, „fără”, „sfert” sau „jumătate”.

Până la minutul treizeci, adăugăm minutele cu ajutorul cuvântului „și”. După minutul treizeci, scădem minutele din ora următoare cu „fără”. Pentru ora două folosim forma de feminin („ora două”), iar pentru numărul unu spunem „ora unu”.
